title: Today vs last week
description: So far today, by hour, against the same weekday a week ago, up to the same time of day.

title: Business snapshot
description: The numbers investors ask for: run rate, growth, retained revenue, what a customer is worth against what one costs, and how fast that pays back.

title: MRR
description: Monthly recurring revenue at the end of each period.
headline: latest

title: MRR movements
description: What added MRR and what took it away in each period.

title: Quick ratio
description: MRR gained for each unit lost: new, expansion and reactivation over contraction and churn. Above 1 the business grows.

title: Revenue per person
description: ARPU is revenue per person active in the period; ARPPU is revenue per person who paid in it.

title: Gross to net
description: What customers paid, split into what you keep, the store's commission, tax and refunds.

title: Effective store fee
description: The store's commission as a share of what customers paid before tax, for each store. Tells you whether you pay the small-business rate.

title: Revenue by store
description: Revenue from each store and payment source.

title: Revenue by product
description: Revenue from the products that earned the most, the rest counted together.

title: Revenue by billing period
description: Revenue by how often the product bills: weekly, monthly, annual or one time.

title: New vs renewal
description: First payments against renewals: how much of the income recurs without winning anyone new.

title: One-time vs subscription
description: Revenue from subscriptions against lifetime and consumable purchases.

title: Revenue by charged currency
description: Revenue by the currency customers were charged in, converted to your reporting currency.

title: Constant-currency revenue
description: Revenue as reported, against revenue at the exchange rates of the start of the period, so the gap is what rates did.

title: Lifetime revenue per customer
description: How many paying customers have brought in how much, after commission and tax.

title: Customer concentration
description: The share of lifetime revenue that the biggest customers brought in.

title: Renewals due
description: Paid subscriptions due to renew in the next 30 days at today's price, and those that will end instead because auto-renew is off.

title: Revenue forecast
description: Expected renewal revenue from today's subscribers over the next 12 months, by how each plan has retained so far. New customers are not in it.

title: Subscribers by plan
description: Active paid subscriptions at the end of each period, by product.

title: Subscriber movements
description: Subscribers gained, won back and lost in each period.

title: Active entitlements
description: People who have each perk now.

title: Shared access
description: Access shared with family members or others in each period.

title: Lifetime value by cohort
description: Cumulative revenue per payer by months since their first purchase, for each month's new payers.

title: Lifetime value by segment
description: Revenue per payer so far, after commission and tax, for each segment.

title: Trial start rate
description: People who started a trial out of those who were shown a paywall.

title: Trial conversion by segment
description: Trials that ended within the period and converted to a paid renewal.

title: When trials cancel
description: The day of the trial on which people turned off auto-renew.

title: Trials ending soon
description: Trials ending in the next 14 days, by whether auto-renew is still on.

title: Subscriber survival by plan
description: The share of those who started paying in the period still subscribed after each month, by plan, counting those too recent to know as still at risk (Kaplan-Meier).

title: Renewal rate by renewal
description: Of the subscriptions due for their first, second, third renewal, how many renewed.

title: What predicts staying
description: New subscribers whose first renewal was decided in the period: those who did one of your events in their first 7 days after paying against those who did not, by how much more often they renewed. An event repeated counts as its own row, and so does being active on 3 or 5 days of that week. Plans renew at different rates, so each event is compared within each plan, but the rates still move with your plan mix: filter by plan to read one on its own. Subscribers still in their first period are left out until it ends, and so are purchases from any store not connected to this project. A correlation, not proof of a cause.

title: Revenue retention
description: Of the MRR at the start of each month, how much was left at its end: net counts upgrades, gross does not.

title: Churn by reason
description: Paid subscriptions that ended in each period, by what happened since their last payment: auto-renew turned off, a failed renewal, or a price increase they were told of.

title: Last active before churn
description: Days between a subscriber's last activity and their subscription ending.

title: Churn by usage
description: Subscribers at the start of the period who churned during it, grouped by how many days they were active in the 30 days before.

title: MRR at risk
description: MRR of active subscribers with auto-renew off, by the week it ends.

title: Billing retry recovery
description: Subscriptions that entered billing retry in each period, by whether they recovered, were lost or are still retrying.

title: Grace period outcomes
description: Subscriptions given a billing grace period in each period, by whether they paid before it ended.

title: Win-backs
description: People who subscribed again after their subscription had ended.

title: Time to win-back
description: Days between a subscription ending and the same person subscribing again.

title: Refund rate by segment
description: Charges in the period that were refunded, for each segment.

title: Refund rate
description: Refunds in each period as a share of the charges in it.

title: Time to refund
description: Days between a charge and its refund.

title: Price increase outcome
description: Subscribers told of a price increase in the period, and what they did about it within 60 days.

title: Offer performance
description: Redemptions of each offer, and how many of those subscribers are still active.

title: Plan switching
description: Subscribers moving between products: upgrades, downgrades and period changes.

title: Active people
description: People active that day, and in the 7 and 30 days up to it. A week or month shows its last day.

title: Stickiness
description: Daily active people as a share of monthly: how habitual the app is. A week or month shows its last day.

title: Days active
description: How many days of the period each active person used the app.

title: People lifecycle
description: In each period, who was new, who returned from the period before, who came back after a gap, and who went dormant. Visitors never identified are left out.

title: Retention cohorts
description: Of the people first seen in each period, the share active again in each period after.

title: Retention by segment
description: The share of new people active again after each day, for each segment.

title: Sessions
description: Sessions in each period. A session ends after 30 minutes without an event.

title: Sessions per person
description: Sessions per active person in each period.

title: Session length
description: Time from a session's first event to its last. A session with one event counts as zero seconds.

title: Time per person
description: Minutes per active person in each period, adding up their sessions' lengths.

title: When people are active
description: Active people by hour of the week, in your time zone.

title: Top screens
description: Screens by views, with the people who saw them and how long they stayed.

title: Time on screen
description: Median time people stay on each screen before moving on.

title: Exit screens
description: The screens sessions most often end on.

title: Paths
description: How people move through the app from a starting screen or event, the most common routes first.

title: Top events
description: Your events by volume, and the share of active people who did each.

title: Event trend
description: Your busiest events over time, or the one you choose.

title: Feature adoption
description: The share of active people who did an event in each period.

title: Time to first action
description: How long new people take from first being seen to first doing an event.

title: What predicts paying
description: New people who did one of your events in their first 7 days, before paying, against those who did not, by how much more often they went on to pay. Events people typically do within an hour of paying are listed last: they are usually steps on the way to the paywall. A correlation, not proof of a cause.

title: People by trait
description: People by the value of a trait you set on them. A value held by fewer than five people is counted under others.

title: Paywall funnel
description: People shown a paywall, those who started a purchase, and those whose purchase completed.

title: Flow drop-off
description: People reaching each screen of a paywall flow.

title: Paywall conversion
description: People who purchased as a share of those shown a paywall, with releases marked so you can see what each change did.

title: Revenue by paywall
description: Revenue credited to what sold it, renewals included.

title: Revenue per 1,000 views
description: The fairest way to compare placements: what each earns per 1,000 people shown it.

title: Sold on a paywall
description: Revenue from purchases made on a paywall, against purchases made elsewhere.

title: Plan mix by paywall
description: Which billing periods each paywall sells.

title: Close-intercept outcome
description: Paywalls that ran an action such as a last offer when someone tried to close them, and whether those people bought within an hour.

title: Price vs conversion by country
description: What buyers pay per month in each country, against how often viewers buy.

title: Experiments
description: Each variant's exposure, conversion and revenue per exposed person, with a check that traffic split as configured.

title: Experiment conversion over time
description: Cumulative conversion of each variant of an experiment.

title: Revenue by acquisition
description: The period's net revenue by the touch credited with each person's signup: paid per network, organic or none.

title: People and revenue by channel
description: What the people each channel brought in went on to do, by the touch credited with their signup.

title: Acquisition funnel
description: People a touch acquired, from visit to payer, each counted on its own surface.

title: Cross-surface journeys
description: The most common routes of payers who moved between the web and an app.

title: Lifetime value by network
description: Net revenue per person by days since their credited touch, for each network.

title: First vs last touch
description: Who opens and who closes: payers and revenue by each person's first and last touch.

title: Touches before paying
description: How many campaign touches payers had before their first purchase.

title: Conversion lag
description: How long people take from one step to the next.

title: Attribution window
description: The same channels at 1, 7 and 28 day windows: how much credit depends on the window.

title: Unattributed revenue by country
description: Revenue from people with no credited touch: where measurement is weakest.

title: How people say they found you
description: Answers to a "How did you hear about us?" question, from the `$acquisition_source` trait.

title: Cost per new payer
description: Ad spend in each period over the people who first paid in it, for connected ad accounts.
headline: latest

title: Blended return
description: All net revenue in each period over all ad spend in it. It needs no attribution, so it is a check on the numbers that do.

title: Predicted payback
description: Return on ad spend by days since the click, as measured and as projected by each plan's retention. The dotted part is the projection.

title: Ad delivery breakdown
description: What Meta reports for the last 28 days, by who and where the ads reached.

title: Traffic
description: Unique visitors, sessions and page views.

title: Bounce rate
description: Sessions that saw a single page.

title: Pages per session
description: Page views per session.

title: Top pages
description: Pages by views, with their visitors, time on page and scroll depth.

title: Landing pages
description: The page each session started on.

title: Exit pages
description: The page each session ended on.

title: Top referrers
description: Other sites sessions arrived from.

title: Campaign traffic
description: Sessions whose landing URL carried campaign parameters.

title: Landing page conversion
description: Visitors who landed on each page, and those who went on to sign up and pay.

title: Web to app handoff
description: Of the identified people an app first reported in the last 7 days, how many were on the web first.

title: Phone, tablet or desktop
description: Sessions by the width of the browser window.

title: Browsers
description: Sessions by browser.

title: Operating systems
description: Sessions by operating system.

title: Web Vitals
description: The 75th percentile of page load (LCP), responsiveness (INP) and layout stability (CLS), as Google's Core Web Vitals measure them.

title: Web Vitals by page
description: The slowest pages by largest paint, at the 75th percentile.

title: Outbound clicks
description: Clicks on links to other sites, by the site they lead to.

title: Installs
description: First launches the SDK reported, by platform. Not store downloads: an app downloaded and never opened is not in it.

title: Install to paying
description: People who installed in the period and how far they have got since it began. A step counts those who reached it or a later one, so someone who pays without a trial is in the trial step too.

title: Lost devices
description: Push tokens the stores reported as no longer valid in each period, the closest signal there is to uninstalls.

title: Version adoption
description: Active people by the app version they used most recently in each period.

title: Updates
description: App updates the SDK reported.

title: Version quality
description: The people who first used each version in the period: how many were active 7 days on, what they paid since and how many had no crash. Did this release hurt?

title: Crash-free people
description: People active in your apps who had no crash reported in each period. With crash events switched off or an older SDK, everyone reads as crash free.

title: Top devices
description: Active people by device model.

title: Device brands
description: Active people by device brand.

title: OS versions
description: Active people by operating system version: when you can drop support for one.

title: Languages
description: Active people by device language.

title: SDK versions
description: The Voidhash SDK versions that reported events in the last 7 days.

title: World map
description: Where your audience and revenue are. Revenue is by store country, so a purchase whose store names none, such as through Stripe, is not on the map.

title: Countries
description: Each country from install to revenue: the audience by where it was active, the money by store country.

title: Opportunity
description: Countries with at least 10 active people, by audience and by how well it pays: big but underperforming markets are at the bottom right.

title: City map
description: Active people by city. A city with fewer than five people is not shown.

title: Cities and regions
description: Active people and sessions by city or region. A place with fewer than five people is not shown.

title: Language by country
description: The most common device language in each country, to show where a translation is missing.

title: Paywall conversion by language
description: People who purchased out of those shown a paywall, by device language. A language with fewer than five viewers is not shown.

title: Store country vs location
description: Payers whose store country differs from where they mostly use the app: moves, VPNs and price arbitrage. A pair of countries with fewer than five payers is not shown.

title: Activity by local time
description: Active people by hour of the week in each person's own time zone.

title: Push delivery
description: Notifications by whether they reached the push provider.

title: Failures by provider
description: Deliveries by push provider, with how many failed.

title: Reachable audience
description: People with a valid push token at the end of each period.
headline: latest

title: Push open rate
description: People who opened a notification out of those it was delivered to.

title: Return after a push
description: People active within 1 and 24 hours of a delivered notification.

title: Revenue after a push
description: Revenue from people within 24 hours of a delivered notification. They may have bought anyway.

title: Events by name
description: Events stored in each period: a sudden drop usually means something broke.

title: Rejected events
description: Events the pipeline could not store, by why.

title: Group types over the limit
description: Events that named a group type beyond the project's 5, by type: those groups were left off them.

title: Event delay
description: Time from an event happening to reaching Voidhash. A long tail is normal for apps used offline.

title: Coverage of payers
description: Paying people the SDK never reported anything for: they declined consent, or the SDK is not identifying them.

title: Webhook success
description: Delivery attempts your endpoints answered successfully.

title: Webhook response time
description: How long your endpoints take to answer.

title: Store notification delay
description: Time from a store reporting a purchase event to Voidhash processing it.
